title: Declarative rollback sentinels and client-side rate limiters for safe rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Add a declarative "sentinel" abstraction to rollout manifests plus client-side pacing and rate-limiter helpers in the SDK so canary/A-B/shadow rollouts can fail fast and auto-rollback with minimal ops intervention. Scope: (1) rollout manifest extension to declare sentinel metrics (latency P50/P95, error-rate, bad-response-rate) and circuit-breaker thresholds; (2) SDK client helper that emits idempotent manifest-seed tokens, applies local rate limits/pacing for canaries, and tags shadow traffic; (3) server-side controller that evaluates sentinel signals, computes confidence windows, and triggers automated rollback hooks when thresholds persist beyond a configurable window. Non-goals: designing the UI for rollout editing (console work tracked separately), reworking core kernel selection, or introducing new telemetry agents. This ticket covers API/SDK primitives and controller hooks + tests and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout manifest accepts a 'sentinels' block with metric name, operator, threshold, window_ms, and severity
SDK exposes an idempotent 'seed_manifest' helper that returns a deterministic token for retries
SDK provides a lightweight client-side rate limiter and pacing helper usable by both hosted and private deployments
Controller evaluates sentinel windows and emits a 'rollback_request' event to the rollout reconciler when conditions persist
Permission scopes prevent non-approved principals from invoking automated rollback or manual force-rollbacks
End-to-end integration test simulating spike in error-rate causes controller to trigger rollback and corresponding audit events logged
API docs and example snippets added to the SDK README and rollout manifest reference

comments: 2026-02-10 - Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to prioritize deterministic idempotency tokens so retries from SDKs are safe. Decision: use HMAC seed tied to manifest id + client seed to avoid stateful server allocations.
2026-02-11 - Liam O'Connor: Implementation note: using a double-buffer sliding window aggregator to avoid locking hot paths in the controller. Will instrument with tracepoints for perf tests.

2026-02-12 - Security review (initial): requested clarification on how seed tokens are validated in Private deployments and whether offline KMS is required. Action: add threat model and key rotation doc to links.

2026-02-13 - PM review (Ana Rodriguez): request to expose 'grace period' on sentinel windows to reduce noise from infra flakiness. Suggested default 3x sample window. Marked as acceptance criteria tweak.
2026-02-14 - Design (Ravi Kapoor): UX note: console will display sentinel health and allow manual 'hold' vs 'rollback' overrides. Will coordinate on API surface for 'hold' signal.
2026-02-15 - Liam O'Connor: PR opened for SDK helpers. Initial benchmarks: client-side limiter adds <1% CPU at 1000 rps, token generation ~200ns per call. Linking PR below.
audit_notes: Every automated rollback emits audit: {actor=controller, reason=sentinel_violation, manifest_id, window_start, window_end, metric_snapshot}
Manual force-rollbacks must include justification and will be rate-limited in console; SDK API returns a 403 if caller lacks 'rollout.rollback' scope
Seed tokens are logged only as truncated identifiers in audit logs to avoid key material leakage
